questions.prompt: Which layer of a web page decides colours, spacing and fonts?
explanations: HTML gives the page its structure: what is there, not how it looks.
Correct: CSS controls how everything looks.
JavaScript adds behaviour, like reacting to clicks.
Git tracks versions of your files. It doesn't style anything.
questions.hint: Structure, style, behaviour: which one is style?

questions.prompt: Spot the bug. Which line breaks this page?
questions.code:
1
2

About me

3

I build things for the web. 4
explanations: The section opens correctly, with an id the nav can link to.
The heading opens and closes properly.

Correct: the paragraph never closes. It should end with

.
The section closes properly.
questions.hint: Every opening tag needs its closing partner.

questions.prompt: What is the best way to mark up the part of your page that lists your projects?
explanations: It works visually, but nothing says what this block is.
Correct: semantic, linkable with #projects, and the verifier finds it.
A footer is for the bottom of the page, like contact details.
A span is for a few words inside text, not a whole part of the page.
questions.hint: Use a tag that says what the block is, plus an id for links.

questions.prompt: Your nav link is Skills. Where does it take the visitor?
options: To the element with id="skills" on the same page
To the first <h2> on the page
Nowhere: links need a full URL
explanations: That would be href="skills.html". A # means a place on the current page.
Correct: # links jump to the element whose id matches.
Links don't look for headings, they look for a matching id.
A # link works without a full URL.

questions.prompt: Put the layers of the CSS box model in order, from the inside out.
explanations: Content in the middle, then padding inside the border, then the border, then margin outside it.
questions.hint: Padding is inside the border, margin is outside.

questions.prompt: Your text is squashed against the edge of its card. Which property adds space inside the card?
explanations: Margin is outside the border: it pushes the whole card away from its neighbours.
Correct: padding is the space between the content and the border.
A thicker border is still a line; it doesn't add breathing room inside.
gap spaces children inside a flex or grid parent, not the text inside a card.
questions.hint: Inside the border or outside it?

questions.prompt: A card has width: 200px; padding: 20px; border: 5px solid. Without box-sizing: border-box, how wide does it look?
explanations: That is only the content. Padding and border are added on top by default.
Only one side of the padding and border was added.
The border was left out: 200 + 20 + 20 = 240, plus 5 on each side.
questions.hint: Add padding and border on both sides.

questions.prompt: You want a gallery of project cards in rows and columns. Which layout fits best?
explanations: Correct: grid lays children out in rows and columns at once.
Block stacks every card on its own line.
You would have to place every card by hand, and it breaks on other screens.
Floats are an old technique and are fragile for layouts.

questions.prompt: Where do you put display: flex to line up three skill badges in a row?
options: On the element that contains the badges
explanations: Flex on a badge arranges what is inside that badge, not the badges themselves.
Correct: the layout is set on the parent, and its children follow.
The body would line up all the page's main blocks, not just the badges.
The head holds information about the page, not visible layout.

questions.prompt: Which CSS creates the frosted-glass blur of what is behind a card?
explanations: filter blurs the card itself, text included.
opacity fades the whole card and blurs nothing.
Correct: backdrop-filter blurs whatever is behind the element.
A shadow adds a glow around the card; the background stays sharp.

questions.prompt: Spot the bug. On a phone this page is tiny and zoomed out. Which line is missing something?
options: There is no viewport meta tag
The style tag must be in the body
explanations: The charset tag is good: it makes special characters display correctly.
Correct: add <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">.
The title only appears in the browser tab. Its length doesn't affect zoom.
Style belongs in the head. That's not the problem.
questions.hint: Phones pretend to be 980px wide unless told otherwise.

options: Applies the CSS inside only on screens 600px wide or narrower
Limits the whole page to 600px wide
Applies the CSS only on screens wider than 600px
explanations: Correct: the rules inside only apply when the screen is at most 600px wide.
That would be max-width on an element, like main { max-width: 600px }.
Media queries are about screens, not video or audio.
That would be min-width: 601px.
